title: Detach grace period, ephemeral output GC, and SDK compatibility shim for streaming disconnects
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem summary:
Customers see two common failure modes when clients disconnect mid-generation: (1) orphaned partial outputs and locked KV-prefixes that waste GPU memory and prevent efficient resumption; (2) client libraries that pre-1.0 do not send disconnect acknowledgements, which prevents the server from making safe cleanup decisions.

Scope and goals:
- Implement a server-side 'detach grace period' where an interrupted generation is soft-detached and retained for a short, configurable window to allow client reconnect and resume.
- Introduce an ephemeral-output GC pipeline that tiers partial outputs by priority and uses adaptive TTL based on workload.
- Add a compatibility shim for older SDKs that don't support a disconnect ACK or lease-renew messages, enabling conservative automatic detachment and metrics.
- Ensure tool/function-calls and structured-output checkpoints are preserved correctly across detach/GC boundaries so that resumed generations do not replay side-effects.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement multi-region cross-account recovery or long-term archival of partial outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes new per-generation metadata: retention_hint (seconds) and detach_lease_id
Default detach grace period = 90s; configurable per-customer; adjustable via Dedicated/Private flags
Orphaned KV-prefixes are released or snapshot to checkpoint store by end of grace period in >= 95% of simulated disconnects
Compatibility shim triggers for SDKs without disconnect ACK and correctly transitions generations to soft-detached state after conservative timeout
No tool/function call side-effects are re-applied when a generation is resumed after soft-detach; system uses idempotency marker on tool calls
End-to-end e2e test that simulates flaky networks, abrupt TCP resets and SDK v0.9 disconnect semantics passes in CI
Dashboard metrics added: orphaned_prefix_bytes, detached_generations_count, avg_grace_retention_seconds, gc_eviction_rate
Operator runbook updated with remediation steps and an automated backfill job to reclaim stuck KV prefixes
technical_notes: Detach model: on client disconnect, mark generation state = SOFT_DETACHED, attach detach_lease_id, schedule a timer = min(retention_hint, customer_max_grace)
Lease renewal: SDKs that support it can renew the detach_lease_id via /streaming/leaseRenew; renewals extend the grace period and bump metric 'lease_renewals'.

KV handling: snapshot KV-prefix to ephemeral checkpoint store if generation contains function-call side-effects. Snapshots are light — only metadata + minimal prefix bytes to enable resume, not full activations.

GC tiers: HOT (clients recently disconnected but with valid detach_lease_id), WARM (no lease, short TTL), COLD (candidate for immediate eviction). Eviction policy prefers reclaiming large orphaned_prefix_bytes first.

Compatibility shim: detect protocol version via handshake header X-RW-SDK-Version; if missing or <1.0.0, set conservative implicit retention_hint = 30s and enable verbose logging for metrics correlation.

Tool-call idempotency: include optional tool_call_id in the generation header; server persists idempotency markers; on resume, tool calls with same id are treated as no-ops and return prior result payload.
Streaming SLO considerations: introduce soft backpressure signals to client (event STREAM_SOFT_DETACHED with recommended reconnect interval) to avoid aggressive retries during GC churn.
Data plane vs control plane: control plane persists detach_lease metadata; data plane performs low-latency snapshotting and eviction. Keep cross-service contracts minimal to reduce latency impact.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy detach_lease handlers and metrics to staging; enable shims for 10% of traffic; run synthetic chaos tests
Phase 2 (limited): enable in us-west-2 for 25% of hosted traffic and all Dedicated sandbox nodes; run automated e2e tests and gather metrics for 48h
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with safe defaults and customer opt-outs; publish SDK guidelines and telemetry docs
Rollback: if orphaned_prefix_bytes increases or resume-success drops by >2% within 6h, rollout paused and revert to previous GC policy
testing_notes: Unit tests for lease state machine and timer transitions
Integration tests for KV snapshot/restore and tool-call idempotency with deliberate duplicate tool_call_id deliveries
Chaos suite: simulate TCP RST, long pauses in streaming (> retention_hint), and flaky SDKs with missing handshake header
Load test: generate 10k concurrent short-lived streams to validate GC memory behavior and eviction ordering
Compatibility tests: run old SDK binaries (v0.8/v0.9) in CI matrix and assert metrics are emitted and soft-detach semantics occur
notes: This design favors short retention to bound cost. For Dedicated customers we will allow per-deployment overrides. Operator tooling (clean-stuck-prefixes) will be provided as an admin job. Plan to coordinate with SDK team for a minor protocol bump that adds explicit disconnect ACK and lease renew endpoints in next SDK release.
